accepted.s: Which fertiliser receives the heaviest subsidy in India?
accepted.x: Urea receives the heaviest fertiliser subsidy. Its price is controlled and kept artificially cheap, encouraging excessive nitrogen use.
accepted.tq: Use the direct one-word identification of the highest-subsidy fertiliser.

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Nutrient Based Subsidy scheme:
1. It was introduced in 2010.
2. It covers 22 grades of decontrolled P&K fertilisers.
3. It fixes the maximum retail prices of P&K fertilisers through the Government.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The scheme was introduced in 2010 for 22 grades of decontrolled P&K fertilisers. Manufacturers set the MRPs of P&K fertilisers themselves, making statement 3 incorrect.
accepted.tq: Find the wrong statement by checking whether pricing remains with manufacturers or the Government.
accepted.sec: Fertiliser subsidy - highest-subsidy fertiliser, NBS, DBT, neem-coated urea, nano urea/DAP, consumption  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following groups consists only of fertilisers covered under the Nutrient Based Subsidy scheme as listed?
o: Urea, ammonium sulphate, MOP and complexes
Urea, SSP, ammonium nitrate and DAP
accepted.x: The listed P&K fertilisers under NBS include DAP, MOP, SSP and complexes. Urea remains under statutory price control rather than the NBS regime.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure exclusion: urea is not part of the listed decontrolled P&K group.
accepted.sec: Fertiliser subsidy - highest-subsidy fertiliser, NBS, DBT, neem-coated urea, nano urea/DAP, consumption  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Under the Nutrient Based Subsidy scheme, the subsidy is announced every year as a fixed amount per kilogram of
accepted.x: NBS provides a fixed per-kilogram subsidy on nitrogen, phosphorus, potassium and sulphur, announced annually.
accepted.tq: Test the exact nutrient composition rather than the broader fertiliser category.
accepted.sec: Fertiliser subsidy - highest-subsidy fertiliser, NBS, DBT, neem-coated urea, nano urea/DAP, consumption  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Under the DBT system for fertilisers, subsidy is paid to companies
o: before manufacture through the Union Budget
after sale at the Point of Sale
accepted.x: Under fertiliser DBT, subsidy is paid to companies after the fertiliser is sold at the Point of Sale (PoS).
accepted.tq: Identify the actual payment trigger in an applied subsidy-disbursement situation.

accepted.s: Neem coating was made applicable to what proportion of domestic urea from 1 September 2015 and imported urea from 1 December 2015?
accepted.x: Neem coating was made mandatory for 100% of domestic urea from 1 September 2015 and imported urea from 1 December 2015.
accepted.tq: Match the exact percentage with the two implementation dates.
accepted.sec: Fertiliser subsidy - highest-subsidy fertiliser, NBS, DBT, neem-coated urea, nano urea/DAP, consumption  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following is NOT a stated effect of neem coating of urea?
o: Reducing misuse of subsidised farm urea
Blocking diversion of farm urea to industry
Increasing the diversion of urea to industry
accepted.x: Neem coating slows nitrogen release and stops diversion of farm urea to industry. It does not increase such diversion.
accepted.tq: Find the reversed cause-effect statement among the stated functions of neem coating.

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. India is the second-largest consumer of fertilisers.
2. India is the third-largest producer of fertilisers.
3. The National Investment Policy for Urea-2026 adds 10 MT of urea capacity.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: India is the second-largest fertiliser consumer and third-largest producer. The National Investment Policy for Urea-2026 adds 10 million tonnes of urea capacity.
accepted.tq: Combine rankings and a capacity figure, checking every statement independently.
accepted.sec: Fertiliser subsidy - highest-subsidy fertiliser, NBS, DBT, neem-coated urea, nano urea/DAP, consumption  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly represents India’s N:P:K fertiliser consumption ratio in 2023–24 and the ideal ratio respectively?
accepted.x: The 2023–24 N:P:K ratio was 10.9:4.1:1, against the ideal ratio of 4:2:1. The imbalance is associated with cheap urea and excessive nitrogen use.
accepted.tq: Keep the observed ratio and the ideal benchmark in their correct order.
accepted.sec: Fertiliser subsidy - highest-subsidy fertiliser, NBS, DBT, neem-coated urea, nano urea/DAP, consumption  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Under PM-PRANAM, approved on 28 June 2023, States receive what share of the fertiliser subsidy saved by reducing chemical fertiliser use?
accepted.x: PM-PRANAM allows States to retain 50% of the subsidy saved through reduced chemical fertiliser consumption.
accepted.tq: Link the scheme’s incentive percentage with its approval date and objective.
accepted.sec: Fertiliser subsidy - highest-subsidy fertiliser, NBS, DBT, neem-coated urea, nano urea/DAP, consumption  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Soil Health Cards:
1. They were launched in 2015.
2. They are issued free of cost every two years.
3. They have been associated with an 8–10% reduction in fertiliser use and a 5–6% rise in yields.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. Soil Health Cards were launched in 2015, are issued free every two years, and are associated with the stated reductions in fertiliser use and increases in yields.
accepted.tq: Verify the date, periodicity and impact figures before selecting the complete combination.
